title: Avionics/Maintenance Technician, Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) (GySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
3. MOS 6314, Avionics/Maintenance Technician, Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS)
(GySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC AVN

    a. Summary. Avionics/Maintenance Technician, Unmanned Aircraft System
(UAS) install, remove, inspect, test, maintain and repair systems components,
and ancillary equipment. These Marines also perform launch recovery and
other flight line operations at the organizational maintenance level.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Must have normal color perception.

            (3) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

            (4) Must possess a CL score of 105 or EL score of 105 or higher.

    c. Requirements. The 63XX OccFld sponsor (ASB-34C) will award the 6314
PMOS to Marines after reviewing necessary qualifications to fulfill initial
qualifiers for Avionics/Maintenance Technicians, Unmanned Aircraft Systems
(UAS).

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (bn), Aviation Maintenance and Supply Training and Readiness
Program (AMSTRP) for MOS 6314.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Avionics Technicians 49-2091.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.
common_text: The avionics OccFld includes direct and indirect support of all aviation weapon systems. While there is a large similarity in the skills required to provide this support, the systems being supported are diverse. The following examples are provided: direct support repair accomplished at the organizational maintenance activity (OMA) which is normally accomplished on aircraft, e.g., replacement of the radar antenna on the aircraft, indirect support-repair accomplished at the intermediate maintenance activity (IMA) which is normally accomplished off aircraft, e.g., radar system module repair, and repair/calibration of the radar support equipment. Marines entering the OccFld receive MOS 6300, Basic Avionics Marine, and then progress through specific hard skill MOSs and ultimately are assigned MOS 6391, Avionics Chief. Qualifications initially include technical proficiency in the repair of one or more electronic systems after completion of formal training. As the Marine is promoted, repair and administrative requirements for multiple systems take on an equal importance until the Marine is ultimately placed in a supervisory position. Billets for both repair and administration are varied and extend from the squadron level to staff positions at the Wing and force commander, and Headquarters U.S. Marine Corps level.

body:
The avionics OccFld includes direct and indirect support of all aviation weapon systems. While there is a large similarity in the skills required to provide this support, the systems being supported are diverse. The following examples are provided: direct support repair accomplished at the organizational maintenance activity (OMA) which is normally accomplished on aircraft, e.g., replacement of the radar antenna on the aircraft, indirect support-repair accomplished at the intermediate maintenance activity (IMA) which is normally accomplished off aircraft, e.g., radar system module repair, and repair/calibration of the radar support equipment. Marines entering the OccFld receive MOS 6300, Basic Avionics Marine, and then progress through specific hard skill MOSs and ultimately are assigned MOS 6391, Avionics Chief. Qualifications initially include technical proficiency in the repair of one or more electronic systems after completion of formal training. As the Marine is promoted, repair and administrative requirements for multiple systems take on an equal importance until the Marine is ultimately placed in a supervisory position. Billets for both repair and administration are varied and extend from the squadron level to staff positions at the Wing and force commander, and Headquarters U.S. Marine Corps level.

3. MOS 6314, Avionics/Maintenance Technician, Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) (GySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC AVN a. Summary. Avionics/Maintenance Technician, Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) install, remove, inspect, test, maintain and repair systems components, and ancillary equipment. These Marines also perform launch recovery and other flight line operations at the organizational maintenance level. b. Prerequisites (1) Must be a U.S. citizen. (2) Must have normal color perception. (3) Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility. (4) Must possess a CL score of 105 or EL score of 105 or higher. c. Requirements. The 63XX OccFld sponsor (ASB-34C) will award the 6314 PMOS to Marines after reviewing necessary qualifications to fulfill initial qualifiers for Avionics/Maintenance Technicians, Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS). d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (bn), Aviation Maintenance and Supply Training and Readiness Program (AMSTRP) for MOS 6314.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
